why: A singly linked list cannot be read backwards, so find the middle with fast/slow pointers, reverse the second half in place, and walk both halves together comparing values. It combines two linked-list moves from this week.
hints: Copying values into an array and comparing with its reverse is O(n) space. The O(1)-space version needs a way to read the back half backwards.
Find the middle with slow/fast pointers, then reverse the list starting at the middle. Now the second half reads from the tail toward the centre.
Compare node by node from head and from the reversed half until the reversed half runs out. O(n) time, O(1) extra space after building the list.
pitfalls: Empty and one-node lists are palindromes.
For odd lengths the middle node needs no partner; stop when the reversed half is exhausted.
Build the list from values first: the exercise asks you to define the node class yourself.
